newsitem.title: NIGER: Eight hurt in Niger coup anniversary clash.
newsitem.headline: Eight hurt in Niger coup anniversary clash.

text.p: Security forces and opposition supporters clashed in north eastern Niger on Monday, on the first anniversary of the coup that brought President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara to power, witnesses said.
At least eight people were hurt in the clashes in the town of Diffa, 1,400 km (950 miles) north east of the capital Niamey, they added.

The opposition, which accuses Mainassara of rigging a July presidential election to consolidate his rule after staging the coup, called for demonstrations across the arid and impoverished nation to mark the anniversary.
Elsewhere, there were no immediate reports of unrest.

Last week, Mainassara freed dozens of opposition activists, including Niger's three main opposition leaders, who were arrested after a banned January 11 opposition protest to demand broader access to state media.
The three, including Mahamane Ousmane, the civilian president Mainassara ousted, were being investigated for threatening state security.

The arrests triggered opposition protests and criticism from abroad. Former colonial power France and the United States, which has denounced Mainassara's election victory as fraudulent, urged their release.
Mainassara supporters easily won November parliamentary elections boycotted by the opposition.
